chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

There is no heart except that it has two ears: upon one of them is a guiding angel, and upon the other is a tempting Satan. This one commands him and this one restrains him. Satan commands him to acts of disobedience, and the angel restrains him from them.
And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Seated on the right and on the left; he does not utter any word except that with him is an observing one, ready.”

key_terms.أُذُنَانِ: two receptive channels through which opposing influences reach the heart
key_terms.بِالْمَعَاصِي: toward acts of disobedience to Allah
key_terms.رَقِيبٌ: a watcher who observes and records
key_terms.شَيْطَانٌ مُفْتِنٌ: a satanic tempter who entices a person toward trial and sin
key_terms.قَلْبٍ: the human heart as the inner center of perception and moral response
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُرْشِدٌ: a guiding angel who directs a person toward right conduct
key_terms.يَزْجُرُهُ: restrains or rebukes him away from wrong

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the angel and Satan influencing the human heart?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that every human heart is subject to two influences: a guiding angel who restrains from sin and a satanic force that incites disobedience. It presents the cited Qur’anic verse as referring to this ongoing moral and spiritual vigilance surrounding human speech and action.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from heart except that there are two ears for it, upon one of the two is a guiding Angel, and upon the other is a tempting Satan<sup>la</sup>. This one instructs him and this one rebukes him. The Satan<sup>la</sup> instructs him with the disobedience and the Angel rebukes him from it,
and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [50:17] seated on the right and on the left [50:18] He utters not a word but there is by him a watcher at hand’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

There is no heart without two ears. On one of them there is an angel who provides guidance and on the other there is a Satan (devil) who induces temptation. This one commands him and that one prohibits him. Satan commands him to disobey and the angel prohibits him from sins

as it is mentioned in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘. . . since the two scribes are sitting on each of his shoulders, he does not utter a word that is not recorded immediately by the watchful scribes.’” [50:17].
